chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any people who revive a portion of the land and develop it, they are more entitled to it, and it belongs to them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on ownership of uncultivated land?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) codifies the principle of *ihya' al-mawat* (revival of dead land), establishing that active cultivation confers superior ownership rights. This ruling serves as a foundational basis for Islamic property law, emphasizing utility and development over mere possession, and remains central to Shia jurisprudence regarding land tenure and agricultural rights.
